name: Battle of Plataea

phases.title: The two lines face each other across the Asopos
phases.text: The Persians lined up north of the river with their left wing facing the Spartans and Tegeans. Next to them stood the Medes and their neighbours, then the Boeotians and other Greek allies of Persia facing the Athenians.

phases.title: The night retreat goes wrong
phases.text: The Greek centre moved off late at night and went too far, ending at the Temple of Hera. The Spartans and Tegeans had not begun to move by daybreak, and a lochos under Amompharetus was left behind. The Athenians were blocked by the scattered centre.

phases.title: The Spartans reach the Temple of Demeter under attack
phases.text: The Spartans and Tegeans reached the Temple of Demeter, and the lochos under Amompharetus began to withdraw from the ridge to join them. The first units of the Persian cavalry started attacking them.

phases.title: Mardonius hurries after the Greeks
phases.text: Mardonius learned of the retreat and rushed to Pausanias's position with the Persian left wing. When the Persian infantry arrived, the cavalry drew back to rest its mounts. The Athenians were engaged by the Boeotians.

phases.title: The Tegeans and Spartans charge
phases.text: The Tegeans ran at the Persian line as arrows fell, and once Pausanias had favourable omens the Spartans charged too. Artabazos brought up 40,000 men in a tight formation, slowly. Amompharetus's men had joined the Spartans.

phases.title: Mardonius is killed and the Persian line breaks
phases.text: Aeimnestus killed Mardonius with a stone. His guards broke and retreated and the rest of the army followed. Artabazos led his men away to Phocis, avoiding the camp.

phases.title: The Athenians outlast the Thebans
phases.text: The Athenians still had to fight the Thebans who stood against them. Eventually the Thebans retreated. Meanwhile the Persian cavalry did not let the Greeks pursue and outflank the retreating Persian army.

phases.title: The Greeks chase the Persians to their camp
phases.text: The Greeks chased the Persians to their camp. The Spartans arrived first and waited for the Athenians, who knew how to scale the walls.

phases.title: The Tegeans breach the camp walls
phases.text: The Tegeans were the first to breach the walls. The Persians could not get into formation and took heavy losses.

note: The Persians stood north of the Asopos and the Greeks south of it, with the Greek right (Spartans and Tegeans) opposite the Persian left, so north is drawn at the top. The Greek centre is drawn staying at the Temple of Hera once it got there, and the Persian cavalry, the camp, Artabazos's men and the places they went to are placed on the side the story needs; the accounts do not give their exact positions. The Greek line moved between positions during the retreat, and the distances given are not all consistent, so the plan shows the order of events, not a survey. Historians give two views of the fighting: that it was a phalanx battle and that the Greeks fought in a looser line; the plan follows the main narrative.
